overall_reason: The single screen is the stock AI-analytics hero: tracked caps eyebrow, headline with one italic word and an accent period, 'AI-powered' sub-line, two CTAs, an invented 3-stat band, a dashboard mock with fake KPIs and 'AI Insight' cards, then a logo strip of famous brands; nothing on it belongs to a specific product.

findings.evidence: Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: 'landing page for an AI analytics tool' yields exactly this: eyebrow 'BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE FOR MODERN TEAMS', h1 'Turn data into decisions, not dashboards.' with italic 'decisions' and a terracotta period, sub-line, 'Start Free Trial' + 'Watch Demo', stat trio, product mock right, logo strip. Cream #fafaf8 page, terracotta accent and an italic display word put it in the warm-paper-serif family's tells (cream_bg, terracotta_accent, eyebrows) applied to a sans.
findings.before: Template split hero with mock and stat trio
findings.after: Lead with one real thing the product does on real data [DATA NEEDED: an actual product screenshot or a named customer's outcome]; drop the eyebrow and the accent-period flourish
findings.why: The page reads as a model's default for the category; a cluster, not one tell.

findings.evidence: Failed T-RIVAL-NAME: put Mode, Hex, Looker or ThoughtSpot in place of 'Meridian' and 'Turn data into decisions, not dashboards.' and 'AI-powered analytics that tells you what matters, when it matters. Less noise, more clarity.' stay true. T-FRESH-READER generic lines: the h1, the sub-line, and 'Trusted by teams at'. The 'X, not Y' and 'Less noise, more clarity' pairs are the stock antithesis rhythm.
findings.after: A headline naming the specific job and user [DATA NEEDED: who uses Meridian and the decision it changes]
findings.why: Concept capped at 5: the whole page holds under a competitor's name.

findings.where: trust bar, bottom of fold: 'Trusted by teams at Stripe Notion Linear Vercel Figma'
findings.evidence: Five famous brand names set as grey text with no logos, links or case studies; the sweep's invented_metrics caught the stats but not this borrowed proof. These are the stock 'logo strip' cast for dev-tool landing pages.
findings.before: Trusted by teams at Stripe, Notion, Linear, Vercel, Figma
findings.after: Remove, or list real customers with permission [DATA NEEDED: actual customer names]
findings.why: Claiming famous customers without evidence is fabricated social proof.

findings.evidence: Dashboard mock with '$2.4M REVENUE', '84.2K USERS', '1.2% CHURN', '$142 ARPU', an unlabelled smooth area line, and cards 'AI Insight: Revenue Acceleration ... grew 23%' and 'Predicted: Q3 Target On Track ... 89% probability'. No axes, no dates, no source; T-DELETION: removing it loses only decoration because none of the data is real.
findings.before: Coded fake dashboard with invented KPIs
findings.after: A real screenshot of the product on demo data labelled as such, or an annotated single view of one insight [DATA NEEDED: product screenshot]
findings.why: A dashboard mock with fake data is a look-family tell the sweep cannot measure and it presents invented figures as product output.

findings.evidence: T-FIVE-SECOND: what it is (BI tool) is answered; for whom ('modern teams') and why this one are not. The page ends after the fold with a 189px empty band and no product, pricing or proof sections, so nav items 'Product', 'Pricing', 'Docs', 'Blog' all point to '#'.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: audience, product sections] then sections a buyer in this category expects (how it works on their data, pricing)
findings.why: The page cannot answer the visitor's next question.

findings.where: above h1: 'BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE FOR MODERN TEAMS'
findings.evidence: T-EYEBROW: covering the 10px tracked-caps eyebrow loses nothing; it repeats the category and duplicates the <title>. The sweep's eyebrow detector did not fire on it (10px span inside .hero-badge).
findings.after: Delete it; put the audience into the sub-line if it is real
findings.why: An eyebrow restating the category is the most common AI hero tell.

strengths: Restrained palette and a single dark primary CTA give a calm first screen; the composition and spacing are competent and worth keeping once real content replaces the mock.
not_investigated: Copy voice: no brand samples supplied.
Lucide icons were shimmed (manifest: 'npm lucide@latest'); icon rendering treated as intended.
